Algebra I · Lesson 9.4

Roots, Sums, and Products

Solve this lesson →All lessons

A monic quadratic with roots rr and ss factors as (x−r)(x−s)(x−r)(x−s), 9.2's factorization written with the roots rather than the search numbers. Expanding gives x2−(r+s)x+rsx2−(r+s)x+rs. Against x2+bx+cx2+bx+c, b=−(r+s)b=−(r+s) and c=rsc=rs, so the roots add to −b−b and multiply to cc. In x2−10x+21=(x−3)(x−7)x2−10x+21=(x−3)(x−7) the roots add to 1010 and multiply to 2121.

Problem
The roots of x2−17x+52x2−17x+52 are rr and ss. Find r+sr+s without factoring the quadratic and without finding either root.
Show a hint
  • Multiply (x−r)(x−s)(x−r)(x−s) out. The coefficient of xx in the expansion is −(r+s)−(r+s).
  • Match that against the coefficient of xx in x2−17x+52x2−17x+52, which is −17−17 with its sign, and solve for r+sr+s.
Show the full solution
Expanding, (x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs(x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs, and matching the middle coefficients gives −(r+s)=−17−(r+s)=−17, so r+s=17r+s=17​. Watch the sign, the coefficient of xx is −17−17, so the sum is its opposite and not −17−17 itself.
Problem
The roots of x2+6x−91x2+6x−91 are rr and ss. Match the quadratic against (x−r)(x−s)(x−r)(x−s) expanded and read off the product rsrs. Enter it as an integer.
Show a hint
  • Match x2+6x−91x2+6x−91 against the expanded form (x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs(x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs. The product of the roots sits in the constant slot.
  • For a second route, factor the quadratic into two whole-number factors, read a root off each factor, and multiply the two roots.
Show the full solution
Matching x2+6x−91x2+6x−91 with (x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs(x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs puts the product in the constant slot, so rs=−91rs=−91​. In x2−(r+s)x+rsx2−(r+s)x+rs the sign flip is on the sum term only, so the constant is the product with no change. Factoring gives (x+13)(x−7)(x+13)(x−7), so the roots are −13−13 and 77, and −13⋅7=−91−13⋅7=−91.
Key idea
Sum and product of the roots. If x2+bx+cx2+bx+c has roots rr and ss, it equals (x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs(x−r)(x−s)=x2−(r+s)x+rs, so r+s=−br+s=−b and rs=crs=c. The sign on the sum is the part that gets misread. In 9.2 the same two letters stood for the search numbers, the constants inside (x+r)(x+s)(x+r)(x+s), and that product is zero at −r−r and −s−s, not at rr and ss. So 9.2's search numbers are the negatives of the roots. The search numbers add to bb, and the roots add to −b−b.
Problem
The numbers 66 and 1717 multiply to 102102 and add to 2323, so x2+23x+102=(x+6)(x+17)x2+23x+102=(x+6)(x+17). What is the sum of the two roots?
Show a hint
  • The two numbers given are the constants inside the factors. A root is a value of xx that makes a factor zero, which is a different thing.
  • x+6x+6 is zero at x=−6x=−6, so the roots are −6−6 and −17−17. Add those, or read −b−b straight off the quadratic.
Show the full solution
The sum of the roots is −b−b, so r+s=−23r+s=−23​. The factors are x+6x+6 and x+17x+17, and x+6x+6 is zero at −6−6, not at 66, so the roots are −6−6 and −17−17, which add to −23−23. Adding the two search numbers instead gives 2323, the right size with the wrong sign.
Problem
The quadratic 8x2+18x−58x2+18x−5 factors as (2x+5)(4x−1)(2x+5)(4x−1). Find its two roots and add them. Enter the sum as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Each factor is zero at one root. Set 2x+5=02x+5=0 and 4x−1=04x−1=0, and solve each one.
  • The roots are −52−25​ and 1441​. Put both over the denominator 44 before adding.
Show the full solution
From (2x+5)(4x−1)(2x+5)(4x−1) the roots are −52−25​ and 1441​, so the sum is −104+14=−94−410​+41​=−49​​. That is −188−818​ reduced, the middle coefficient over the leading one with the sign flipped, which is not a coincidence.
Key idea
Any leading coefficient. Divide ax2+bx+c=0ax2+bx+c=0 through by aa, which is not zero, and what remains is x2+bax+ca=0x2+ab​x+ac​=0. Dividing both sides of an equation by a nonzero number changes no solution, so this quadratic has the same two roots, and the monic rule applies to it as written. Then r+s=−bar+s=−ab​ and rs=cars=ac​. The last problem is the check. For 8x2+18x−58x2+18x−5 the sum is −188=−94−818​=−49​ and the product is −58−85​. When a=1a=1 these are −b−b and cc again.

Both facts are read off the coefficients in place. Put the quadratic in standard form with one side zero, and aa, bb and cc are already written down. For 6x2−13x−36x2−13x−3 the sum of the roots is −−136=136−6−13​=613​ and the product is −12−21​. Nothing was factored, and this one has no integer factorization to find.

Problem
A monic quadratic has two roots that add to 1212 and multiply to −85−85. Write it in the form x2+bx+cx2+bx+c and enter bb, the coefficient of xx.
Show a hint
  • A monic quadratic with roots rr and ss is (x−r)(x−s)(x−r)(x−s), which expands to x2−(r+s)x+rsx2−(r+s)x+rs. Line that up against x2+bx+cx2+bx+c.
  • Matching the xx terms gives −b=r+s−b=r+s, and the roots add to 1212. Solve that for bb.
Show the full solution
The roots add to −b−b, so −b=12−b=12 and b=−12b=−12​. The quadratic is x2−12x−85x2−12x−85, which is (x−17)(x+5)(x−17)(x+5) with roots 1717 and −5−5. Writing 1212 straight in as the coefficient of xx gives x2+12x−85x2+12x−85, whose roots add to −12−12 instead.
Problem
One root of 5x2−16x+3=05x2−16x+3=0 is 33. Find the other root from the sum of the roots rather than by factoring, and enter it as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • The two roots add to −ba−ab​, and one of them is already known, so the other is one subtraction away.
  • The sum is 165516​. Subtract 33 from it. Dividing the product 3553​ by 33 is the second route.
Show the full solution
The roots add to −−165=165−5−16​=516​, so the other root is 165−3=15516​−3=51​​. The product gives the same value, 35÷3=1553​÷3=51​.
Key idea
Building a quadratic from its roots. Given a sum SS and a product PP, the monic quadratic with those two numbers as its roots is x2−Sx+Px2−Sx+P, since that is (x−r)(x−s)(x−r)(x−s) expanded with r+s=Sr+s=S and rs=Prs=P. The coefficient of xx is the negative of the sum and the constant is the product, which is the monic rule read backwards. Multiplying by any nonzero number gives another quadratic with the same two roots, and x2−Sx+Px2−Sx+P is the only monic one.

Here is what the two facts are for. Some expressions in rr and ss can be rewritten so that only r+sr+s and rsrs appear in them, and any expression like that can be evaluated from aa, bb and cc alone. Whether the roots are integers, fractions, or numbers no method in this chapter produces makes no difference to the work.

Problem
The quadratic 7x2−5x−97x2−5x−9 has no factorization with integer coefficients, so nothing in this chapter produces its roots. Call them rr and ss anyway and find 1r+1sr1​+s1​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Combine the two fractions over the common denominator rsrs. The result is a sum divided by a product, and both of those come from the coefficients.
  • The sum is 5775​ and the product is −97−79​. Divide the first by the second, and the sevens cancel.
Show the full solution
Over the common denominator rsrs, 1r+1s=r+srsr1​+s1​=rsr+s​. Here r+s=57r+s=75​ and rs=−97rs=−79​, so the value is 5/7−9/7=−59−9/75/7​=−95​​. The sevens cancel in the division, so this expression is −bc−cb​ for any quadratic with cc not zero, whatever aa is.
Fun fact
Albert Girard stated the relations between a polynomial's coefficients and its roots in 1629, in general form and for any degree. He gave the pattern without a proof, before notation had settled enough to write it cleanly.
Problem
The roots rr and ss of x2−5x−8=0x2−5x−8=0 are not integers, so factoring will not produce them. Find r2+s2r2+s2 from the sum and the product of the roots alone.
Show a hint
  • Neither root can be found here, but r+sr+s and rsrs come straight from the coefficients. Build r2+s2r2+s2 out of those two numbers.
  • Squaring r+sr+s gives r2+2rs+s2r2+2rs+s2, which is 2rs2rs too big. Here rs=−8rs=−8, so watch the sign when you subtract 2rs2rs.
Show the full solution
Since (r+s)2=r2+2rs+s2(r+s)2=r2+2rs+s2, subtracting 2rs2rs gives r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rsr2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs. Here r+s=5r+s=5 and rs=−8rs=−8, so the value is 25−2(−8)=25+16=4125−2(−8)=25+16=41​. The product is negative, so −2rs−2rs is positive here. Reading it as 25−16=925−16=9 is the standard slip.
Key idea
Symmetric expressions. An expression in rr and ss is symmetric when swapping the two letters leaves it unchanged. Both r2+s2r2+s2 and 1r+1sr1​+s1​ are symmetric. Symmetric expressions can almost always be rewritten with only r+sr+s and rsrs in them, so the value comes from the coefficients. Four rewritings are enough here. Over a common denominator, 1r+1s=r+srsr1​+s1​=rsr+s​. Since (r+s)2=r2+2rs+s2(r+s)2=r2+2rs+s2, subtracting 2rs2rs leaves r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rsr2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs, and then (r−s)2=r2+s2−2rs=(r+s)2−4rs(r−s)2=r2+s2−2rs=(r+s)2−4rs. Last, r2s+rs2=rs(r+s)r2s+rs2=rs(r+s).

The coefficients are the shorter route even when the roots are findable. 20x2+x−1220x2+x−12 factors as (4x−3)(5x+4)(4x−3)(5x+4), so one way to reach 1r+1sr1​+s1​ is to add 4334​ and −54−45​ over a common denominator. From the coefficients it is −bc−cb​, a single division.

Problem
The quadratic 2x2−15x+c2x2−15x+c has two roots, and one of them is four times the other. Neither root is given. Find the value of cc.
Show a hint
  • Call one root rr, so the other is 4r4r. Their sum is −ba−ab​, so the stated ratio gives one equation in one unknown.
  • The sum of the roots is 152215​, so 5r=1525r=215​. Once both roots are known, use the product, which is c22c​ rather than cc.
Show the full solution
Call the roots rr and 4r4r. They add to 152215​, so 5r=1525r=215​ and r=32r=23​, making the roots 3223​ and 66. Their product is 99, and the product of the roots is c22c​, so c=18c=18​. The slip here is reading that product as cc rather than c22c​, which gives 99.
Problem
The two roots of x2−24x+cx2−24x+c differ by 88. Call them rr and ss, and find the value of cc without finding either root.
Show a hint
  • Both (r+s)2(r+s)2 and (r−s)2(r−s)2 expand to r2+s2r2+s2 plus or minus 2rs2rs, so (r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs.
  • For x2−24x+cx2−24x+c the sum of the roots is 2424 and the product is cc, and the squared difference is 6464. Put all three into that identity.
Show the full solution
Here r+s=24r+s=24 and rs=crs=c, so (r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs becomes 64=576−4c64=576−4c, and c=128c=128​. The difference r−sr−s is not symmetric and cannot be read off the coefficients, but (r−s)2(r−s)2 is, which is what makes this work. A sum of 2424 and a difference of 88 also give the roots outright, 1616 and 88.
Key idea
Working backwards, and where it stops. A stated fact about the roots is one equation in r+sr+s and rsrs, and solving it gives the unknown coefficient. With a fixed ratio between the roots, the sum is linear in one unknown. A stated difference is squared first, since (r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs. Equal roots mean r=sr=s, so the product is r2r2. On their own the two facts never produce the roots, and for some sums and products no real pair exists. For sum 22 and product 55, (r−s)2(r−s)2 would be 4−20=−164−20=−16, and no real square is negative. Chapter 11 takes up x2−2x+5x2−2x+5.

Any question that involves the roots only through r+sr+s and rsrs can be answered from the coefficients, and there is exactly one monic quadratic with a stated sum and product. Neither fact separates rr from ss, and neither one produces a root. The last two problems use most of the lesson at once.

Problem
The quadratic 4x2+10x−214x2+10x−21 has no integer factorization, so no method in this chapter produces either root. Its roots are rr and ss. Find r2s+rs2r2s+rs2 as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • Both terms have a factor of rsrs. Take it out and see what is left.
  • r2s+rs2=rs(r+s)r2s+rs2=rs(r+s), with rs=−214rs=−421​ and r+s=−52r+s=−25​. Two negatives multiply to a positive.
Show the full solution
Both terms have a factor of rsrs, so r2s+rs2=rs(r+s)r2s+rs2=rs(r+s). Here r+s=−104=−52r+s=−410​=−25​ and rs=−214rs=−421​, so the value is (−214)(−52)=1058(−421​)(−25​)=8105​​. Both factors are negative, so the value is positive. A sign dropped anywhere in the setup shows up as −1058−8105​.
Problem
Let rr and ss be the roots of 4x2−12x−94x2−12x−9, which does not factor over the integers. Find the coefficient of xx in the monic quadratic whose roots are r2r2 and s2s2, as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show a hint
  • In a monic quadratic the coefficient of xx is the negative of the sum of its roots, and the roots here are r2r2 and s2s2, so find r2+s2r2+s2 first.
  • From the coefficients, r+s=3r+s=3 and rs=−94rs=−49​. Use r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rsr2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs, then flip the sign of the result.
Show the full solution
From the coefficients, r+s=124=3r+s=412​=3 and rs=−94rs=−49​, so r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs=9−2(−94)=272r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs=9−2(−49​)=227​. The monic quadratic with roots r2r2 and s2s2 is x2−(r2+s2)x+r2s2x2−(r2+s2)x+r2s2, so its coefficient of xx is −272−227​​. Neither root was needed anywhere in that. The sign flip is the step to watch, since 272227​ is the sum of the new roots and the coefficient is its negative.

Every answer in this lesson's second half came off the coefficients, and four of those quadratics have no root chapter 9 can produce. Lesson 9.5, Factoring in Action, turns these tools on equations not written as ax2+bx+c=0ax2+bx+c=0. An equation can be a quadratic in some repeated piece, and naming that piece with one letter makes it one you can solve.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Find the sum of the two roots of x2−15x+26=0x2−15x+26=0. Read the sum off the coefficients, and keep the sign of the middle coefficient in mind.
Show the solution
The coefficient of xx is b=−15b=−15, so the sum of the roots is −b=−(−15)=15−b=−(−15)=15​. Factoring gives the same total, since x2−15x+26=(x−2)(x−13)x2−15x+26=(x−2)(x−13) and 2+13=152+13=15.
Practice
The quadratic x2−33−8xx2−33−8x is not written in standard form. Put it in standard form, then find the product of its two roots. The leading coefficient is 11, so the product can be read straight off once it is.
Show the solution
The quadratic is monic, so the product of the roots is its constant term, rs=−33rs=−33​. Check by factoring, x2−8x−33=(x−11)(x+3)x2−8x−33=(x−11)(x+3), whose roots 1111 and −3−3 multiply to −33−33.
Practice
The quadratic x2+19x+34x2+19x+34 factors as (x+2)(x+17)(x+2)(x+17). Find the sum of its two roots. Read each root off its own factor first, and mind the sign as you do it.
Show the solution
The factors x+2x+2 and x+17x+17 are zero at −2−2 and −17−17, so the two roots add to −19−19​. Both roots are negative, so the sum is the negative of the middle coefficient 1919, never 1919 itself.
Practice
Find the product of the two roots of 10x2+11x−6=010x2+11x−6=0. Give your answer as a fraction in lowest terms. The leading coefficient is not 11 here, so the constant term alone is not the product.
Show the solution
The product of the roots is ca=−610=−35ac​=10−6​=−53​​. As a check, 10x2+11x−6=(5x−2)(2x+3)10x2+11x−6=(5x−2)(2x+3) has roots 2552​ and −32−23​, and 25⋅(−32)=−3552​⋅(−23​)=−53​.
Practice
Find the sum of the two roots of 8x2+30x−78x2+30x−7 as a fraction in lowest terms. This quadratic has no integer factorization, so the sum has to come from the coefficients.
Show the solution
The sum of the roots is −ba=−308=−154−ab​=−830​=−415​​. The roots themselves are irrational, so no factor search would have found them, and the sum is still exact.
Practice
A monic quadratic has two roots that add to −6−6 and multiply to −40−40. Enter the coefficient of xx in that quadratic. The two roots themselves are not needed.
Show the solution
The roots add to −b−b, so −b=−6−b=−6 and b=6b=6​. The quadratic is x2+6x−40=(x+10)(x−4)x2+6x−40=(x+10)(x−4), with roots −10−10 and 44, which add to −6−6 and multiply to −40−40.
Practice
One root of the quadratic x2−2x−63x2−2x−63 is 99. Find the other root from the sum of the roots rather than by factoring, then check it against the product.
Show the solution
The roots add to −(−2)=2−(−2)=2, so the other root is 2−9=−72−9=−7​. Checking against the product, 9⋅(−7)=−639⋅(−7)=−63.
Practice
One root of 6x2−19x+146x2−19x+14 is 22. The leading coefficient is 66, not 11, so the two roots add to −ba−ab​ rather than to −b−b. Find the other root as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
With a=6a=6 and b=−19b=−19, the roots add to −ba=196−ab​=619​, so the other root is 196−2=76619​−2=67​​. The product route gives the same value, since the roots multiply to ca=73ac​=37​ and 73÷2=7637​÷2=67​.
Practice
The quadratic 5x2−14x+45x2−14x+4 has no integer factorization. Its roots are rr and ss. Find 1r+1sr1​+s1​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Over a common denominator, 1r+1s=r+srsr1​+s1​=rsr+s​. Here r+s=145r+s=514​ and rs=45rs=54​, so the value is 144=72414​=27​​. The fifths divide out, so for any ax2+bx+cax2+bx+c this expression equals −bc−cb​, with b=−14b=−14 and c=4c=4 here.
Practice
Let rr and ss be the roots of the quadratic x2−9x+11x2−9x+11, neither of which is an integer. Find r2+s2r2+s2 without finding either root.
Show the solution
Since the quadratic is monic, r+s=9r+s=9 and rs=11rs=11, so r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs=81−22=59r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs=81−22=59​. Expanding (r+s)2(r+s)2 gives r2+2rs+s2r2+2rs+s2, which exceeds r2+s2r2+s2 by exactly 2rs2rs, so one subtraction of 2rs2rs is the whole correction.
Practice
Let rr and ss be the roots of the quadratic x2−6x−2x2−6x−2, which does not factor over the integers. Find (r−s)2(r−s)2.
Show the solution
(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs=36−4(−2)=36+8=44(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs=36−4(−2)=36+8=44​. The product rsrs is negative, so −4rs−4rs is positive here, and the common slip is 36−8=2836−8=28.
Practice
Is there a pair of real numbers rr and ss whose sum is 44 and whose product is 99? Decide from the square of their difference, which is fixed by the sum and the product alone, then answer yes or no.
Show the solution
For such a pair, (r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs=16−36=−20(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs=16−36=−20, and no real number has a negative square, so the answer is nono​. The quadratic with that sum and product is x2−4x+9x2−4x+9, and chapter 11 takes it up.
Practice
Both roots of x2+bx+125x2+bx+125 are negative, and one root is five times the other. Start from the product of the roots rather than the sum. Find bb.
Show the solution
With roots rr and 5r5r, the product is 5r2=1255r2=125, so r=−5r=−5 since both roots are negative, and the roots are −5−5 and −25−25. They add to −30−30, and the sum of the roots is −b−b, so b=30b=30​. Taking r=5r=5 gives two positive roots and b=−30b=−30 instead.
Practice
Both roots of 25x2−40x+c25x2−40x+c are the same number. Find cc. The leading coefficient is not 11, so use the sum and the product in their general form.
Show the solution
The roots sum to −ba=4025=85−ab​=2540​=58​, and equal roots are each half of that, so each is 4554​. Their product 16252516​ equals c2525c​, so c=16c=16​. Checking, 25x2−40x+16=(5x−4)225x2−40x+16=(5x−4)2.
Practice
The quadratic x2−14x+cx2−14x+c has two roots that differ by 44. The difference itself cannot be read off the coefficients, but its square can. Find cc.
Show the solution
Here r+s=14r+s=14 and rs=crs=c, so (r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs(r−s)2=(r+s)2−4rs becomes 16=196−4c16=196−4c and c=45c=45​. As a check, the roots must be 99 and 55, since those sum to 1414 and differ by 44, and their product is 4545.
Practice
Let rr and ss be the roots of 2x2−5x−62x2−5x−6, which does not factor over the integers. Find rs+srsr​+rs​ as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
Over a common denominator, rs+sr=r2+s2rssr​+rs​=rsr2+s2​. From the coefficients, r+s=52r+s=25​ and rs=−3rs=−3, so r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs=254+6=494r2+s2=(r+s)2−2rs=425​+6=449​, and the value is 494÷(−3)=−4912449​÷(−3)=−1249​​. Because rsrs is negative, the −2rs−2rs term is +6+6 and not −6−6, which is the usual slip here.
Practice
Let rr and ss be the roots of x2−7x+3x2−7x+3, which does not factor over the integers. Build the monic quadratic whose roots are 1rr1​ and 1ss1​, and enter its coefficient of xx as a fraction in lowest terms.
Show the solution
From the coefficients, r+s=7r+s=7 and rs=3rs=3, so the new roots add to 1r+1s=r+srs=73r1​+s1​=rsr+s​=37​, and a monic quadratic's coefficient of xx is the negative of the sum of its roots, so it is −73−37​​. The built quadratic is x2−73x+13x2−37​x+31​.
